Back-end-of-line — the wiring layers abo: Aluminum, replaced by IBM's copper interconnect process in the late 1990s.

What does 'BEOL' stand for?: Why does copper conduct better than aluminum?
Back-end-of-line — the wiring layers abo: Copper's resistivity is about 40% lower, and it resists electromigration better under high current density.

What does 'BEOL' stand for?: Why can't copper be plasma-etched like aluminum?
Back-end-of-line — the wiring layers abo: Copper does not form volatile etch byproducts under standard plasma chemistries — it cannot be cleanly removed that way.

What does 'BEOL' stand for?: What barrier metal is deposited before the copper seed layer, and what does it prevent?
Back-end-of-line — the wiring layers abo: Tantalum nitride (TaN) — it prevents copper from diffusing into surrounding silicon or dielectric materials.

What does 'BEOL' stand for?: What is CMP, and what role does it play in dual-damascene?
Back-end-of-line — the wiring layers abo: Chemical-mechanical polishing — it removes the excess copper deposited above the trenches, leaving only the inlaid wires.

What does 'BEOL' stand for?: What is the wire pitch of the lowest metal layers (M1/M2) at a leading-edge node?
What is 'low-k dielectric' and why is it used between metal layers?
Back-end-of-line — the wiring layers abo: A dielectric with relative permittivity below ~2.5 (versus 3.9 for SiO₂), used to reduce capacitive coupling between adjacent wires and speed signal propagation.
